Write a scale as a definition file, and read one back

Source: R/definition.R
write_scale.Rd

A definition is a header (JSON, the stored form; YAML on request) plus tables. A small scale fits in one file with every table inline; a large one is a bundle directory holding scale.json and its tables as Arrow IPC files (or CSV when arrow is not installed). Either form is language-neutral: the header is plain JSON and the tables are Arrow or CSV with their column types recorded.

write_scale(
  x,
  path,
  format = c("json", "yaml"),
  tables = c("auto", "inline", "arrow", "csv"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

read_scale(path, package = NULL, class = c("stored", "core"))

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

path

A file (.json, .yaml, .yml) or a bundle directory; for read_scale() also a catalogue id.

format

Header format: "json" (default) or "yaml". A single-file path fixes it by its extension.

tables

Where the tables go: "auto" (inline when the tables hold at most 1000 rows in all, else "arrow" when arrow is installed, else "csv"), "inline", "arrow" or "csv". A single file can only inline.

overwrite

Replace a definition already at path.

package

For a catalogue id: the package whose definition to take when several packages ship the same id.

class

"stored" (default) returns the class recorded in the header; "core" the plain NestedScale.

Value

write_scale() returns path, invisibly. read_scale() returns the scale.

Details

path ending in .json, .yaml or .yml writes a single file; any other path is a bundle directory. A bundle is only ever written into an empty directory or over a bundle written before (overwrite = TRUE); nothing else in a directory is touched.

read_scale() takes a file, a bundle directory, or the id of a shipped definition (see scale_catalog()). The scale comes back as the class it was written from when that class is registered (see register_scale_class()); class = "core" asks for the plain NestedScale instead, dropping any payload.

Round trips

An arrow bundle reads back identical. A JSON or YAML header carries numbers at 15 significant digits, so an inline table reads back equal (all.equal()), not necessarily identical, for arbitrary doubles.

Examples

s <- scale_example()
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "example.json")
write_scale(s, f, overwrite = TRUE)
back <- read_scale(f)
identical(scale_frames(back), scale_frames(s))
#> [1] TRUE
all.equal(scale_leaftable(back), scale_leaftable(s))
#> [1] TRUE

# a bundle, with the tables as files
if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- file.path(tempdir(), "example.scale")
  write_scale(s, d, tables = "arrow", overwrite = TRUE)
  list.files(d)
  identical(scale_leaftable(read_scale(d)), scale_leaftable(s))
}
#> [1] TRUE
